cls: Thiazolidinedione (TZD) oral antidiabetic; PPAR-gamma agonist (insulin sensitiser)
pharm: Activates PPAR-gamma, increasing insulin sensitivity in adipose, muscle, and liver

Onset of glycemic effect is slow (weeks)

Take with or without food (consistent timing)

Avoid - excreted in animal milk; not recommended

Limit - additive effect on glycemic control / hepatic risk

summary: Rosiglitazone is a thiazolidinedione (TZD) oral antidiabetic that acts as a selective agonist of the nuclear receptor PPAR-gamma, reducing insulin resistance in adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, and liver to improve glycemic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus. The usual dose is 4 mg/day (once daily or split), increasing to a maximum of 8 mg/day; its glucose-lowering effect develops slowly over weeks. It carries a BOXED WARNING that thiazolidinediones, including rosiglitazone, may cause or worsen congestive heart failure through fluid retention - it is contraindicated in NYHA Class III-IV heart failure and patients must be monitored for edema, weight gain, and dyspnoea. Other notable risks include an increased rate of bone fractures (particularly in women), macular edema, and hepatic effects (avoid in active liver disease). Its ischemic cardiovascular safety has been the subject of regulatory scrutiny and prescribing restrictions.
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus - as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control, as monotherapy or in combination with metformin or a sulfonylurea (where appropriate)

dosage.d: 4 mg/day as a single daily dose or in two divided doses (2 mg twice daily)
dosage.t: Assess response after 8-12 weeks (glycemic effect is delayed)
dosage.n: Lower starting dose if added to a sulfonylurea/insulin (hypoglycaemia/edema risk)

dosage.d: May increase to 8 mg/day (once daily or 4 mg twice daily) if inadequate response after 8-12 weeks
dosage.t: 8 mg/day twice-daily dosing may give greater HbA1c reduction

dosage.d: 4 mg/day, increasing to 8 mg/day as needed
dosage.n: No metformin dose change required for rosiglitazone

dosage.d: 4 mg/day; if edema or hypoglycaemia occurs, reduce the sulfonylurea
dosage.t: Use 8 mg only with close monitoring

dosage.d: Do not initiate if ALT >2.5x ULN; check LFTs before starting
dosage.t: Recheck if ALT rises; discontinue if jaundice or ALT >3x ULN persists

admin: Take once daily or in two divided doses, with or without food, consistently
Obtain baseline liver function tests (ALT) before starting and periodically thereafter
Do not initiate if ALT is greater than 2.5 times the upper limit of normal
Assess for heart failure risk and symptoms (edema, rapid weight gain, dyspnoea) before and during treatment
Expect a delayed glycemic effect - evaluate response over 8-12 weeks before titrating
Reduce the dose of co-administered insulin or sulfonylurea if fluid retention or hypoglycaemia develops
moa: Rosiglitazone is a highly selective and potent agonist of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-gamma (PPAR-gamma), a nuclear receptor expressed in insulin-sensitive tissues (adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, liver). Activation of PPAR-gamma regulates transcription of genes involved in glucose and lipid metabolism, increasing insulin sensitivity. The result is enhanced insulin-dependent glucose uptake in muscle and adipose tissue and decreased hepatic glucose output, lowering blood glucose without directly stimulating insulin secretion. Because it depends on the presence of insulin for its effect, rosiglitazone is ineffective in the absence of insulin (e.g. type 1 diabetes). PPAR-gamma activation also promotes sodium/fluid retention, underlying the edema and heart-failure risk.

absolute: NYHA Class III or IV heart failure (established congestive heart failure)
Known hypersensitivity to rosiglitazone or any component
relative: NYHA Class I or II heart failure or other risk factors for heart failure
Active hepatic disease or ALT >2.5x ULN at baseline
History of ischemic cardiac disease (cardiovascular safety concerns)
Pre-existing edema or on other fluid-retaining drugs (NSAIDs, insulin)
Osteoporosis or high fracture risk (especially postmenopausal women)
Premenopausal anovulatory women (may resume ovulation - pregnancy risk)
monitor: Liver function tests (ALT) at baseline and periodically
Signs/symptoms of heart failure - edema, weight gain, dyspnoea

preg: There are no adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women; rosiglitazone should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Because abnormal blood glucose during pregnancy is associated with congenital anomalies and increased neonatal morbidity, most experts recommend insulin to maintain glucose control during pregnancy rather than oral agents. Note that rosiglitazone may induce ovulation in anovulatory premenopausal women, increasing the chance of pregnancy.
lact: Rosiglitazone-related material was detected in the milk of lactating rats; it is not known whether it is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk and of the potential for adverse effects, rosiglitazone should not be administered to a breastfeeding woman.
renal: No dose adjustment is required for rosiglitazone itself in renal impairment, as it is extensively metabolised by the liver. However, rosiglitazone should not be used together with metformin in patients with significant renal impairment (because of metformin's contraindication), and fluid-retention effects warrant caution.
hepatic: Rosiglitazone is metabolised by the liver. Do not initiate therapy if the baseline ALT is greater than 2.5 times the upper limit of normal, and avoid use in patients with active liver disease. Check liver enzymes before starting and periodically thereafter; if ALT rises to >3x ULN, recheck and discontinue if it persists or if jaundice develops.

major: Insulin (increased risk of fluid retention, edema, and congestive heart failure - combination generally not recommended/avoided)
Nitrates (combination with rosiglitazone associated with increased ischemic events in some analyses)
moderate: Strong CYP2C8 inhibitors e.g. gemfibrozil (markedly raise rosiglitazone levels - reduce dose / monitor)
Strong CYP2C8 inducers e.g. rifampin (lower rosiglitazone levels)
Other antidiabetics - sulfonylureas/insulin (hypoglycaemia, additive fluid retention)
NSAIDs (additive sodium/fluid retention and heart-failure risk)
interactions.food: No clinically significant food effect; may be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Limit - alcohol can disturb glycemic control and adds hepatic risk
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a dilutional fall in hemoglobin/hematocrit; monitor ALT and HbA1c

serious: New or worsening congestive heart failure (BOXED WARNING)
Bone fractures (especially upper arm, hand, foot in women)
Hepatotoxicity (rare elevations; avoid in active liver disease)
Possible increased risk of myocardial ischemia (debated; subject of regulatory review)
rare: Ovulation in anovulatory premenopausal women leading to unintended pregnancy
emergency: Acute decompensated heart failure / pulmonary edema

monitoring: Liver function tests (ALT) at baseline and periodically
Signs and symptoms of heart failure: peripheral edema, rapid weight gain, breathlessness
Visual symptoms suggestive of macular edema
Bone mineral density / fracture risk in at-risk patients
counsel: Report swelling of ankles/legs, rapid weight gain, or shortness of breath at once (heart failure)
This medicine lowers blood sugar slowly - it may take a few weeks to see the full effect
Attend liver blood tests as scheduled; report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or nausea/vomiting
Be aware of an increased risk of bone fractures, especially in women - support bone health
Report any new blurred vision or visual changes (possible macular edema)
If you are a premenopausal woman with irregular periods, this drug may restore ovulation - use contraception if pregnancy is not desired
Limit alcohol and continue diet, exercise, and glucose monitoring
pk: Glycemic effect is gradual - measurable over 1-2 weeks, maximal effect by ~8-12 weeks
Plasma Cmax approximately 1 hour after an oral dose
Store at 20-25 degrees C (excursions 15-30 degrees C); protect from light and moisture
pearls: BOXED WARNING: thiazolidinediones, including rosiglitazone, may cause or worsen congestive heart failure via fluid retention - contraindicated in NYHA Class III-IV; monitor for edema, weight gain, dyspnoea.
Glycemic effect is delayed - do not judge response or titrate before 8-12 weeks.
Increases bone fracture risk, especially in women; can cause macular edema and dilutional anemia.
Cardiovascular ischemic safety has been controversial (REREMS restrictions were later relaxed by FDA); avoid combining with insulin (edema/heart failure) and use cautiously with nitrates/NSAIDs.
Hepatically cleared via CYP2C8 - gemfibrozil markedly raises levels; do not start if ALT >2.5x ULN.
Source note: a clean openFDA label was not retrievable for rosiglitazone; this record is based on the FDA-approved Avandia (rosiglitazone maleate) prescribing information and standard references.
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your usual schedule. Do not take a double dose. Keep taking it regularly, as the blood-sugar benefit depends on consistent use.
overdose: Information on overdose is limited. Manage according to the patient's clinical status with supportive care. Because rosiglitazone is highly protein bound, it is not expected to be cleared by hemodialysis. Monitor for fluid retention/heart failure and hypoglycaemia (particularly if taken with insulin or a sulfonylurea), and treat symptomatically.
